senses.title: Break a hard solid on purpose
senses.definition: to break or crack a hard material such as rock, metal or glass
senses.definitionCN: 使岩石、金属、玻璃等坚硬材料破裂或出现裂缝
senses.example: A geologist uses a chisel to fracture the core sample.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家用凿子敲裂岩芯样品。
senses.why: fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from frangere, to break; the verb is the act that produces a fractura.
senses.whyCN: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，源自动词 frangere「打破」；动词义就是产生一道断裂的动作。

senses.title: The crack that results
senses.definition: a crack or line of breakage in a solid object
senses.definitionCN: 固体物件上出现的裂缝或断线
senses.example: A hairline fracture ran across the marble slab.
senses.exampleCN: 一条发丝般的细裂缝横过大理石板。
senses.why: Latin fractura named both the act and its result, and English kept the same double life in one noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fractura 同时指动作与结果，英语把这个双重身份原样保留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Break a bone
senses.definition: to crack or break a bone in the body
senses.definitionCN: 使身体中的骨头裂开或折断
senses.example: He fractured his wrist when he fell off the ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，手腕骨折了。
senses.why: a bone is the hardest solid in the body, so the general sense of breaking a hard thing settled naturally on bone.
senses.whyCN: 骨头是身体里最硬的固体，因此「敲断硬物」的一般义自然落在骨折上。

senses.title: A break in the rock mass
senses.definition: a planar break through rock along which the two sides have moved or can move
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿岩层、两侧已发生或可能发生位移的破裂面
senses.example: The fault is a fracture that has slipped many times.
senses.exampleCN: 这条断层是一条多次滑动的破裂面。
senses.why: geology took the everyday noun and made it precise: a fracture is any break, a fault is one that has actually slipped.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把日常名词精确化：fracture 泛指破裂，fault 专指真正发生过滑动的那一条。

senses.title: Split a group into camps
senses.titleCN: 使团体分裂成对立阵营
senses.definition: to divide a group, party or alliance into opposing parts
senses.definitionCN: 使团体、政党或联盟分裂为对立的几部分
senses.example: The dispute fractured the alliance into three camps.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端把联盟分裂成三个阵营。
senses.why: the image of a solid breaking into pieces was transferred from stone to social bodies, which also lose their wholeness.
senses.whyCN: 固体碎成数块的意象被移用到社会群体上，因为群体同样会失去完整。

senses.title: A split in unity or agreement
senses.definition: a division or breach in something previously united, such as trust or consensus
senses.definitionCN: 原本统一之物（如信任或共识）出现的分裂或缺口
senses.example: The report exposed a fracture in the coalition's common position.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告暴露出联盟共同立场上的一道裂口。
senses.why: the noun sense extends the physical crack to anything that can no longer be described as one piece.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把物理裂缝扩展到一切不再能被称作「一整块」的事物。

senses.title: The way a mineral breaks
senses.definition: the characteristic surface shape a mineral shows when it breaks other than along cleavage planes
senses.definitionCN: 矿物不沿解理面断开时所呈现的特征断面形态
senses.example: Quartz shows a conchoidal fracture rather than flat cleavage.
senses.exampleCN: 石英呈现贝壳状断口，而不是平整的解理面。
senses.why: mineralogy needed a word for the surface left by breaking, and fracture already meant exactly that result.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学需要一个词指断裂留下的表面，而 fracture 本来就表示这个结果。

senses.title: Break the continuity of something abstract
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：打断某种连续性
senses.definition: to break the continuity or smooth working of a system, narrative or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 打断系统、叙事或关系的连续性或顺畅运转
senses.example: One missing shipment can fracture a delicate supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 一次缺货就可能打断一条脆弱的供应链。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the core gesture: something that was continuous is now interrupted by a break.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留核心动作：原本连续的东西，如今被一道断口打断。

intro.en: Fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from the verb frangere, to break, whose past participle is fractus. The word entered English in the fifteenth century, first as the medical name for a broken bone.
intro.cn: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，出自动词 frangere「打破」，其过去分词为 fractus。该词于 15 世纪进入英语，最初是骨折的医学名称。

items.en: Frangere meant to break, shatter or smash. Its past participle fractus supplied the stem frac- seen in fracture, fraction and fragment.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破、击碎、砸碎」。其过去分词 fractus 提供了 fracture、fraction、fragment 中所见的 frac- 词干。

items.en: Fractura was the noun of result, a breaking or the breach produced by it, used for broken bones as well as broken objects.
items.cn: fractura 是结果名词，指「断裂」或断裂造成的破口，既用于断骨，也用于破碎的物件。

items.en: English took fracture in the fifteenth century as a term for a broken bone, alongside the older verb break.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借入 fracture，作为骨折的术语，与更古老的动词 break 并存。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to rock masses and to manufactured materials, where a fracture is a plane of breakage.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，该词被用于岩体与人工材料，其中 fracture 指一个破裂面。

items.en: In modern usage a society, party or narrative can be fractured, extending the stone image to anything that loses its wholeness.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，社会、政党或叙事都可以被 fracture，把石头的意象扩展到一切失去完整性的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the link of frangere to a reconstructed Indo-European root for breaking is a standard reconstruction, not a recorded form; the first date of the geological sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：frangere 与重构的印欧语「打破」词根之间的联系属于标准重构，并非有记录的形式；地质义的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin breaking stock; group two holds near neighbours that also describe damage or division.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「打破」词干的词；第二组是同样表示损坏或分裂的近义词。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: cracked, split or disjointed, as in a fractured skull or a fractured story.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的过去分词作形容词：裂开的、分裂的、支离破碎的，如骨折的头骨或破碎的叙事。

entries.definition: From the same frangere stock: a piece broken off something larger, so it names the result rather than the break.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 frangere：从更大物体上掉下的一块，指结果而非断裂本身。

entries.definition: Also from fractus, but it shifted to a numerical part of a whole and no longer means a physical break.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 fractus，但语义转向「整体的数值部分」，不再指物理断裂。

entries.definition: From frangere through French: easily broken, describing a quality rather than an event.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自 frangere：容易破碎的，描述性质而非事件。

entries.definition: A narrow line of breakage or a sharp splitting sound; it can be smaller than a fracture and need not separate the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的裂线或清脆的爆裂声；可以比 fracture 更轻，且两半不必分离。

entries.definition: The general English verb for separating into pieces; fracture is its technical and medical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示分成数块的一般英语动词；fracture 是它技术化、医学化的对应词。

entries.definition: To divide along a line, often cleanly, as wood splits; it stresses separation rather than shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 沿一条线分开，常指干脆地劈开，如木头裂开；强调分离而非碎成多块。

entries.definition: A sudden tearing or bursting of something under pressure, such as a pipe or a tendon; it adds force to the idea of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 受压之物突然撕裂或爆开，如管道或肌腱；在「断裂」之上加了「受力爆裂」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: frac- is the broken stem: frangere broke things, and fractus is the broken result.
normal.cn: frac- 就是「断」的词干：frangere 打破东西，fractus 是打破的结果。

normal.en: The family runs fracture, fractured, fracturing, fraction, fragment, fragile and refract.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fracture、fractured、fracturing、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

normal.en: Medical phrases fix the bone sense: hairline fracture, stress fracture, compound fracture.
normal.cn: 医学搭配固定了骨折义：细微骨折、应力性骨折、开放性骨折。

normal.en: Geology pairs it with fault and fracture zone, where the break is a plane in rock.
normal.cn: 地质学把它与断层、断裂带配对，此时断口是岩体中的一个面。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: fracture a bone, fracture a rock, fracture an alliance.
normal.cn: 动词直接带宾语：使骨折、敲裂岩石、使联盟分裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fract（断）+ ure」——像石头被敲出一道缝 → 断裂、骨折、分裂

root: 拉丁 frangere「打破」的过去分词 fractus + 名词后缀 -ura → fractura「断裂」；英语 fracture。同族含 fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: a hard thing loses its wholeness. The event is then named as a noun, located in bone, made a plane in rock, and finally applied to groups, agreements, mineral surfaces and systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个事件展开：坚硬之物失去完整。这个事件先被名词化，再落到骨头、岩体中的平面，最后用于群体、共识、矿物断面与系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound slab that acquires a sharp new line and is no longer one piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块完好的石板出现一道锋利的新线，从此不再是一整块。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the verb names the blow, the noun names the line it leaves.
branches.cn: 动作与结果：动词指那一下敲击，名词指它留下的那条线。

branches.en: BONE: the body's hardest solid is the most personal place a fracture can happen.
branches.cn: 骨头：身体里最硬的固体，是断裂最能切身发生的地方。

branches.en: ROCK AND MINERAL: geology turns the break into a measurable plane or surface.
branches.cn: 岩石与矿物：地质学把断裂变成可测量的平面或断面。

branches.en: SOCIAL SPLIT: a group, like a slab, can lose its wholeness along a line.
branches.cn: 社会分裂：群体和石板一样，会沿一条线失去完整。

branches.en: SYSTEM BREAK: continuity itself is what snaps in the abstract use.
branches.cn: 系统中断：抽象用法里断掉的是连续性本身。

intro.en: Fracture is a Latin noun of result built from a verbal stem plus a suffix, and the same stem recurs across English.
intro.cn: fracture 是由动词词干加后缀构成的拉丁结果名词，同一词干在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere, fractus and fractura give fracture, fraction, fragment, fragile, refract and frangible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frangere、fractus 与 fractura 衍生 fracture、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract 与 frangible。

items.example: The stem frac- carries the result of breaking.
items.exampleCN: 词干 frac- 承载「打破之后的结果」。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing

items.exampleCN: fractura 是在分词之上构成的结果名词。

items.example: The chisel fracture left a clean edge.
items.exampleCN: 凿出的断裂留下干净的边。

items.meaningCN: 断裂的；分裂的；支离破碎的
items.example: The fractured rock face showed several sets of joints.
items.exampleCN: 断裂的岩面显出好几组节理。

items.example: Hydraulic fracturing opened the shale.

items.meaning: a breaking into parts, hence a numerical part
items.meaningCN: 分成部分，后指数值上的分数
items.example: Only a fraction of the sample survived.
items.exampleCN: 样品中只有一小部分留存。

items.example: Fragments of the core lay on the bench.
items.exampleCN: 岩芯的碎片散在实验台上。

items.example: The fragile shell cracked at a touch.

items.meaning: to bend a ray back as it passes
items.example: Water refracts the light entering it.
items.exampleCN: 水使进入其中的光发生折射。

items.example: The frangible target shattered on impact.

definition_en: a small broken piece, an incomplete part, or to break into pieces

definition_en: a border or structure, to put a picture in a frame, to plan, or to make someone seem guilty
core_image: 一圈木条围住照片，把画面固定在里面
scene: 他把照片装进相框，挂在墙上。He put the photo in a frame and hung it on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 frame 是「相框、框架」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把照片装进相框，挂在墙上。

senses.title: A border or structure
senses.definition: a border around a picture or a structure that supports something
senses.definitionCN: 照片四周的边框，或支撑某物的结构
senses.example: He put the photo in a frame and hung it on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把照片装进相框，挂在墙上。
senses.why: This is the basic supporting-border sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的支撑边框义项。

senses.title: To put in a frame
senses.definition: to put a picture or document inside a frame
senses.definitionCN: 把照片或文件装进框里
senses.example: She framed the old map.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张旧地图装进了框里。
senses.why: The noun became an action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化成了动作。

senses.title: To plan
senses.definition: to shape or plan something carefully
senses.definitionCN: 仔细设计或构思某事
senses.example: They framed a new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们制定了一项新政策。
senses.why: A structure is planned before it is built.
senses.whyCN: 结构在建成之前先被设计。

senses.title: To make someone seem guilty
senses.definition: to make an innocent person seem guilty
senses.definitionCN: 让无辜的人显得有罪
senses.example: Someone framed him for the theft.
senses.exampleCN: 有人陷害他盗窃。
senses.why: A false picture is built around a person.
senses.whyCN: 有人围绕一个人搭建虚假的图画。

abstract.en: To frame is to choose a boundary.

branches.en: A wooden frame holds the photo.

definition_en: honest and direct in what you say

scene: 说实话，我不喜欢这个计划。To be frank, I don't like the plan.

senses.title: Honest and direct

senses.definitionCN: 不掩饰地说出真实想法
senses.example: To be frank, I don't like the plan.

senses.why: This is the basic honesty sense.

senses.title: Open and plain

senses.why: An open face matches open words.

definition_en: to become ice, to stop something, to feel very cold, or a period of frost
core_image: 寒夜里湖面慢慢结出一层白冰
scene: 湖面在一夜寒风中冻住了。The lake froze in the cold night wind.
sceneCN: 这里 freeze 是「结冰」（第 1 个义项）；句意：湖面在一夜寒风中冻住了。

senses.title: To turn into ice
senses.definition: to become hard and solid because of cold
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷而变硬变实
senses.example: The lake froze in the cold night wind.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面在一夜寒风中冻住了。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of water turning to ice.
senses.whyCN: 这是水变成冰的基本义项。

senses.title: To stop something
senses.definition: to stop money, prices, or activity from moving
senses.definitionCN: 使资金、价格或活动停止变动
senses.example: The company froze all new spending.
senses.exampleCN: 公司冻结了所有新的开支。
senses.why: Something frozen cannot move, so stopping movement borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 冻住的东西不能动，于是「停止」也借用了这个词。

senses.title: To feel very cold
senses.definition: to feel extremely cold
senses.definitionCN: 感到极度寒冷
senses.example: My hands are freezing in this wind.

senses.why: The body feels like it is turning to ice.
senses.whyCN: 身体感觉像要结成冰。

senses.title: A period of frost
senses.definition: a time when the weather stays below freezing
senses.definitionCN: 天气持续低于冰点的时期
senses.example: The freeze lasted for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 冰冻期持续了两周。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun for the cold period itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，指寒冷期本身。

definition_zh: 摩擦；摩擦力；由摩擦产生的热与磨损；人与人之间的龃龉
definition_en: the resistance that arises when one surface moves against another, or the tension between people or groups
core_image: 两只手掌用力对着搓，掌纹之间冒出细碎的热与屑
scene: 两位同事为一份预算反复修改，会上说话越来越短。Friction between the two colleagues slowed the project to a crawl.
sceneCN: 这里 friction 指人与人之间不断擦碰而产生的紧张（第 5 个义项：人际间的龃龉）；句意为两位同事之间的摩擦使项目慢得几乎停住。图中可辨识物件：摊开的预算表、两支笔、半杯冷掉的茶、关着的会议室门。

derivatives.zh: 摩擦音；摩擦音的（同一词根）

senses.title: The act of rubbing surfaces together
senses.titleCN: 两个表面相互擦过的动作
senses.definition: the act of two surfaces rubbing against each other while one or both move
senses.definitionCN: 一个或两个表面移动时相互擦过的动作
senses.example: The friction of the rope against the rail wore a groove in the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子与栏杆的摩擦在木头上磨出一道沟。
senses.why: Latin fricare meant to rub, and its noun frictio named the rubbing itself before it named any force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fricare 意为「摩擦」，其名词 frictio 先指「擦」这个动作，之后才指一种力。

senses.title: The force that opposes sliding
senses.titleCN: 阻碍两表面相对滑动的力
senses.definition: the force produced when two surfaces in contact move against each other and resist the motion
senses.definitionCN: 两个接触面相互移动时产生并阻碍该运动的力
senses.example: Engineers added a low-friction coating to the piston.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给活塞加了一层低摩擦涂层。
senses.why: Once the rubbing was studied as a quantity, the noun shifted from the action to the resistance it produces.
senses.whyCN: 当人们把这种擦动当作一个量来研究，名词就从动作转到它所产生的阻力。

senses.title: Heat and wear from rubbing
senses.definition: the heat or damage that rubbing produces on a surface or between parts
senses.definitionCN: 擦动在表面或部件之间产生的热或损伤
senses.example: The friction of the drill bit scorched the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 钻头摩擦把木头烫焦了。
senses.why: Rubbing two things together makes them warm and wears them down, so the word came to name the effects as well as the cause.
senses.whyCN: 两物相互擦会发热并损耗，于是这个词既指原因，也指结果。

senses.title: A rasping sound of rubbing
senses.definition: the harsh sound made when rough surfaces are drawn across each other
senses.definitionCN: 粗糙表面相互擦过时发出的刺耳声响
senses.example: The friction of the bow on the strings filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 弓在弦上的摩擦声充满了大厅。
senses.why: The ear hears the rubbing as noise, which is the same event described through another sense.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵把这种擦动听成声响，这仍是同一件事，只是换了一个感官来描述。

senses.title: Tension between people
senses.definition: a feeling of tension or annoyance between people who rub against each other's habits
senses.definitionCN: 人们因习惯相互擦碰而产生的紧张或恼怒
senses.example: Friction between the two colleagues slowed the project to a crawl.
senses.exampleCN: 两位同事之间的摩擦使项目慢得几乎停住。
senses.why: Two people who irritate each other are pictured as surfaces scraping, and the eighteenth-century figurative use made this sense common.
senses.whyCN: 相互惹恼的两个人被想象成两个相擦的表面，十八世纪以后的比喻用法使这一义流行起来。

senses.title: Disagreement that slows work
senses.titleCN: 使事情办不下去的意见不合
senses.definition: disagreement over plans or terms that makes cooperation difficult and slow
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或条件上的分歧，使合作变得困难而缓慢
senses.example: There was friction over who would pay for the repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 在由谁出修缮费的问题上出现了摩擦。
senses.why: When talks scrape instead of glide, the image moves from private annoyance to a dispute that blocks a joint task.
senses.whyCN: 当谈判不再是顺畅滑行而是相擦，画面就从私人的恼怒转到挡住共同事务的争执。

senses.title: Resistance inside a system
senses.titleCN: 系统或流程内部消耗的阻力
senses.definition: anything in a process, market or machine that makes movement slower or costlier
senses.definitionCN: 流程、市场或机器中使运转更慢或代价更高的一切因素
senses.example: The app was designed to remove friction from the checkout.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的设计目的是消除结账环节的阻力。
senses.why: Modern usage treats any drag in a flow as friction, borrowing the mechanical word for costs and delays.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把流动中的任何拖拽都视为摩擦，用这个机械词来指成本与延误。

senses.title: Conflict between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体或阶层之间的冲突
senses.definition: repeated conflict or resentment between social groups that live or work in contact
senses.definitionCN: 接触密切的社会群体之间反复发生的冲突或怨气
senses.example: Friction between the two communities rose after the water shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水之后，两个社群之间的摩擦加剧了。
senses.why: Communities that share a border rub against each other constantly, so the word widens from persons to whole groups.
senses.whyCN: 共享边界的社群不断相互擦碰，于是这个词从个人扩大到整个群体。

intro.en: Friction comes from Latin frictio 'a rubbing', from fricare 'to rub'; the deeper origin of fricare is uncertain, and the figurative sense for quarrels grew after the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: friction 来自拉丁 frictio「摩擦」，出自 fricare「摩擦、揉搓」；fricare 的更早来源不确定，指人际龃龉的比喻义是十八世纪以后长出来的。

items.en: Fricare meant to rub or chafe; its own earlier origin is uncertain, so no deeper root is claimed here.
items.cn: fricare 意为「摩擦、揉搓」；它更早的来源不确定，因此这里不声称更深的词根。

items.en: Frictio was the noun of that verb, naming a rubbing or the soreness left by it.
items.cn: frictio 是那个动词的名词，指一次摩擦或擦后留下的疼痛。

items.en: The word entered English through learned Latin and French, first as a term for rubbing and later for the resistance between surfaces.
items.cn: 这个词经学术拉丁语与法语进入英语，先指摩擦动作，后指表面之间的阻力。

items.en: Mechanics gave friction a measured place among forces, which fixed the physical sense of the word.
items.cn: 力学把摩擦列入可测量的力之中，固定了这个词的物理义。

items.en: Writers then applied the scraping image to quarrels and social life, producing the interpersonal sense.
items.cn: 随后作家把这种相擦的画面用到争吵与社交生活上，产生了人际义。

items.en: The first dates for the figurative senses are approximate; the mechanical sense is well recorded in the early modern period.
items.cn: 比喻义的最早年代为约数；机械义在近代早期已有明确记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like friction; the second group names neighbouring kinds of rubbing, drag and disagreement.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 friction 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「摩擦、阻力、不和」说法。

entries.definition: A part of a whole or a number below one; it comes from Latin frangere 'to break', a different root, and only sounds like friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体的一部分或小于一的数；来自拉丁 frangere「打破」，与 friction 不同源，只是音近。

entries.definition: A break in bone or rock; from Latin frangere 'to break', with no link to rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指骨头或岩石的断裂；来自拉丁 frangere「打破」，与摩擦无关。

entries.definition: A consonant made by forcing air through a narrow gap; the name comes from the same verb for rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指气流挤过窄缝发出的辅音；名称出自同一个表示摩擦的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective of friction, used of forces, heat and unemployment that arise from rubbing or drag.
entries.definitionCN: friction 的形容词，用于由摩擦或阻力产生的力、热与失业。

entries.definition: Invented writing; it comes from Latin fingere 'to shape or feign', not from the verb for rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指虚构作品；来自拉丁 fingere「塑造、假装」，并非出自那个表示摩擦的动词。

entries.definition: Wear or a scraped wound caused by rubbing on a hard surface.
entries.definitionCN: 因与硬面摩擦造成的磨损或擦伤。

entries.definition: Any force or refusal that opposes motion; friction is one specific mechanical kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻碍运动的任何力或抗拒；摩擦是其中一种具体的机械类型。

entries.definition: The resistance of air or water to a moving object, or anything that slows progress.
entries.definitionCN: 指空气或水对运动物体的阻力，也指拖慢进展的事物。

entries.definition: Strain between people or groups that may break into conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或群体之间可能爆发为冲突的紧张。

entries.definition: Open disagreement and a lack of harmony, stronger and more audible than friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开的分歧与不和谐，比 friction 更强、更外显。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fricare is Latin for to rub, so friction is rubbing before it is a force.
normal.cn: fricare 是拉丁语「摩擦」，所以 friction 首先是「擦」这个动作，然后才是一种力。

normal.en: The family runs frictional, frictionless, frictionally and the phonetic term fricative.
normal.cn: 同族词有 frictional、frictionless、frictionally 以及语音学术语 fricative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: reduce friction, friction between, friction costs.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：减少摩擦、……之间的摩擦、摩擦成本。

normal.en: Physicists separate static friction, which holds a body still, from kinetic friction, which acts while it slides.
normal.cn: 物理学家把使物体停住的静摩擦与滑动时起作用的动摩擦区分开来。

normal.en: The deeper origin of fricare is uncertain, so no further root should be invented for it.
normal.cn: fricare 更早的来源不确定，不应为它编造更深的词根。

abstract.en: Picture two palms pressed together and rubbed hard until they feel warm.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌压在一起用力搓，直到发热。

abstract.en: Picture a stubborn drawer that screeches every time it is pulled.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倔强的抽屉，每次拉动都发出刺耳的响声。

abstract.en: Picture two people who agree on the plan but sigh at every sentence the other says.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同意同一个计划，却对对方每句话都要叹一口气。

examples.en: Less friction in the bearing meant the motor ran cooler.
examples.cn: 轴承里的摩擦减少，意味着马达运转得更凉。

examples.en: The report blamed friction between agencies for the delayed response.
examples.cn: 报告把响应迟缓归咎于机构之间的摩擦。

examples.en: Repeated friction with the same neighbor can wear down a whole community.
examples.cn: 与同一邻居反复摩擦，会磨损整个社群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗里克申」——两人一擦就生热，话不投机就起摩擦

root: 拉丁 fricare「摩擦、揉搓」→ 拉丁 frictio「摩擦」→ 英语 friction；fricare 更早的词源不确定，人际龃龉义是十八世纪后的比喻用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scrape: surfaces rub, the rub turns into a force, into heat and wear, into noise, then into the scrape between people, between plans, inside a system and between whole groups.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次擦碰：表面相互擦过，擦动变成一种力，又变成热与磨损、声响，随后变成人与人、计划与计划、系统内部以及群体之间的擦碰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms pressed together and rubbed until they feel warm and gritty.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手掌压在一起用力搓，直到发热、发涩。

branches.en: THE SCRAPE ITSELF: before any force is named, the word simply describes two surfaces drawn across each other.
branches.cn: 擦本身：在指任何力之前，这个词只是描述两个表面相互擦过。

branches.en: THE FORCE MEASURED: the scrape becomes a quantity that engineers can reduce or use.
branches.cn: 被测量的力：擦动变成一个工程师可以减小或利用的量。

branches.en: WHAT THE SCRAPE LEAVES: warmth, wear and a harsh sound are the same event felt by skin and ear.
branches.cn: 擦动留下的东西：热、磨损与刺耳声，是同一件事被皮肤和耳朵感到的样子。

branches.en: BETWEEN PEOPLE AND PLANS: two habits scrape, and a shared task slows down.
branches.cn: 人与计划之间：两种习惯相擦，共同的任务就慢下来。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND GROUPS: any drag in a flow, and any repeated conflict between communities, takes the same name.
branches.cn: 系统与群体：流动中的任何拖拽、社群间任何反复冲突，都用同一个名字。

intro.en: Friction is built from a Latin verb for rubbing and a noun ending, and the same verb supports several English words.
intro.cn: friction 由一个表示摩擦的拉丁动词和一个名词词尾构成，这个动词还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fricare gives friction and the phonetic term fricative; the exact deeper source of fricare is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fricare 衍生 friction（摩擦）与语音学术语 fricative（摩擦音）；fricare 更早的确切来源不确定。

items.example: The ending turns the verb of rubbing into a noun.

items.example: The Latin noun first names the act, not a force.

items.example: The English noun later takes on the measured mechanical sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词后来承担了可测量的机械义。

items.example: The adjective is used of forces, heat and unemployment.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于力、热与失业。

items.example: The suffix describes a surface or a process with no drag at all.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀描述完全没有阻力的表面或流程。

items.example: The adverb names the manner in which something is driven.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词说明某物被驱动的方式。

items.example: Phonetics borrows the rubbing image for air forced through a gap.
items.exampleCN: 语音学借用了这个摩擦画面，指气流被挤过窄缝。

definition_en: to make someone afraid, or to drive someone away by fear
core_image: 雷声响起，孩子猛地缩起肩膀
scene: 突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。The sudden thunder frightened the child.

senses.title: To force by fear

senses.definitionCN: 通过恐惧使某人做某事
senses.example: They frightened him into signing the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们吓得他签了文件。
senses.why: Fear can push a person into action.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧能推着人行动。

definition_en: white ice crystals on cold surfaces, or freezing weather
core_image: 清晨的草叶上结着细细的白霜
scene: 清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。A layer of frost covered the grass in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 frost 是「霜」（第 1 个义项）；句意：清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。

senses.title: White ice crystals
senses.definition: thin white ice that forms on cold surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 在寒冷表面形成的薄白冰晶
senses.example: A layer of frost covered the grass in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。
senses.why: This is the basic weather sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的天气义项。

senses.title: Freezing weather
senses.definition: a period of weather cold enough to damage plants
senses.definitionCN: 冷到足以冻坏植物的天气时段
senses.example: An early frost ruined the young shoots.
senses.exampleCN: 一场早霜毁了嫩芽。
senses.why: The white crystals stand for the cold that makes them.
senses.whyCN: 白霜代指造成它的寒冷。

senses.title: Icing on a cake
senses.definition: a sweet coating on baked food
senses.definitionCN: 烘焙食品表面的甜涂层
senses.example: The cake was covered with white frosting.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上覆着一层白糖霜。
senses.why: The white coating looks like frost on a cold surface.
senses.whyCN: 白色涂层看起来像冷面上的霜。

abstract.en: Frost is silence made visible.
abstract.cn: 霜是看得见的寂静。

abstract.en: Cold writes gently on every surface it touches.
abstract.cn: 寒冷在触及的每个表面上轻轻书写。

abstract.en: What freezes overnight can melt by noon.
abstract.cn: 一夜冻结之物，正午便可融化。

root: 源自古英语 forst（霜），属日耳曼语，核心义「寒冷表面凝结的白色冰晶」。

sensesIntro.en: Frost means white ice crystals, freezing weather, or icing on a cake.

core.en: Cold made white on a surface.
core.cn: 寒冷在表面上凝成的白色。

branches.en: Grass wears a thin white coat.

definition_en: to pull your eyebrows together, showing displeasure or deep thought
core_image: 老师皱着眉低头看作业本
scene: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
sceneCN: 这里 frown 是「皱眉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。

senses.title: Pull the brows together
senses.definition: to move your eyebrows together because you are angry, worried, or thinking hard
senses.definitionCN: 因生气、担忧或苦苦思索而把眉毛皱在一起
senses.example: The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
senses.exampleCN: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。
senses.why: This is the basic facial action the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词所指的基本面部动作。

senses.title: Show disapproval
senses.definition: to disapprove of something, often used with on or upon
senses.definitionCN: 不赞成某事，常与 on 或 upon 连用
senses.example: Many parents frown on late-night phone use.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家长不赞成深夜玩手机。
senses.why: A frown signals that something is not acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 皱眉表示某事不被接受。

senses.title: The frown itself
senses.definition: an expression in which the brows are pulled tightly together
senses.definitionCN: 双眉紧锁的表情
senses.example: A deep frown crossed his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上掠过一道深深的皱眉。
senses.why: The action can also be named as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作也可以作为一个名词来称呼。

intro.cn: frown 从古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Fruitful describes heavy branches, good results, or a productive life of work.
sensesIntro.cn: fruitful 形容果实压枝、结果良好，或创作多产。

core.en: Full of fruit, and therefore full of results.

branches.en: A talk yields useful decisions.
branches.cn: 一次谈话产生有用的决定。

branches.en: Branches bend under heavy fruit.

branches.en: A writer's years produce many works.
branches.cn: 作家的岁月产生许多作品。

branches.en: Harvest and creative output share one image.

definition_zh: 挫败感；挫折；受阻；使（计划）落空
definition_en: the feeling or state of being blocked, or the act of making an effort or plan come to nothing
core_image: 一个人反复拧一颗已经滑丝的螺丝，手指越用力，螺纹越是空转
scene: 实验台前的学生第七次把同一段线路接上又拆下，示波器上的波形始终是乱的，他把工具往桌上一放。Frustration showed in the way the student pushed the breadboard away after another failed attempt.
sceneCN: 这里「挫折感」指「努力被反复挡住后生出的无力与烦躁」（第 1 个义项：受阻而生的情绪）；句意为又一次尝试失败后，这名学生把电路板推开，挫败感显露出来。

pos.zh: 挫败感；挫折；受阻（不可数指情绪，可数指造成挫败的事）

derivatives.zh: 使受挫；使落空（拉丁动词「使成为徒劳」直接进入英语）
受挫的；沮丧的（动词过去分词转为形容词）
令人挫败的（动词现在分词转为形容词，指引起这种感受）

senses.title: The feeling of being blocked
senses.definition: the unpleasant feeling that comes when effort meets a barrier and cannot get through
senses.definitionCN: 努力遇到阻碍、无法通过时产生的不快感受
senses.example: Frustration rose in her voice as the form was rejected for the third time.
senses.exampleCN: 表格第三次被退回时，她声音里的挫败感升了上来。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make vain', so the feeling is what a vain effort leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使成徒劳」，因此这种感受就是徒劳的努力留下的东西。

senses.title: An obstacle that blocks
senses.definition: something that keeps a person from reaching a goal, viewed as a cause rather than a mood
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人达到目标的障碍物，被视为成因而非情绪
senses.example: Traffic was the first frustration of an already difficult morning.
senses.exampleCN: 对本来就不顺的早晨来说，交通是第一个挫折。
senses.why: The same word names the barrier and the reaction to it, because one produces the other.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指障碍又指对它的反应，因为前者产生后者。

senses.title: Making a plan come to nothing
senses.definition: the act of defeating an aim or a scheme, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 使某个目标或计策失败，常带刻意成分
senses.example: The frustration of the proposal by two committee members cost a year of work.
senses.exampleCN: 两名委员让提案落空，代价是一年的工作。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of the Latin noun: rendering something useless, whether by accident or by design.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁名词最古老的意思：使某物变得无用，无论出于偶然还是有意。

senses.title: A run of repeated failure
senses.definition: an extended period in which attempts keep failing, treated as an experience rather than a moment
senses.definitionCN: 一段不断失败的经历，被当作经历而非瞬间
senses.example: Years of frustration in the laboratory finally produced a working method.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里多年屡屡受挫，最终产生了一套可行的办法。
senses.why: Repetition turns a single blocked moment into a stretch of time with its own weight.
senses.whyCN: 重复把一次受阻的时刻拉成一段自有重量的时间。

senses.title: Pent-up irritation
senses.definition: irritation that has accumulated because it cannot be expressed at the moment it arises
senses.definitionCN: 因为当时无法表达而积累起来的恼怒
senses.example: He threw the pen across the desk in pure frustration.
senses.exampleCN: 他纯粹出于积压的烦躁把笔摔到了桌子那头。
senses.why: Blocked energy has to go somewhere; when it cannot reach the goal, it turns into temper.
senses.whyCN: 被挡住的力量总要有去处；到不了目标，就变成脾气。

senses.title: The frustration-aggression link
senses.titleCN: 挫折与攻击的心理学术语
senses.definition: in psychology, the state of being prevented from reaching a goal, studied as a trigger of aggression
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，被阻止达到目标的状态，被研究为攻击行为的触发因素
senses.example: The study tested the frustration-aggression hypothesis with a simple puzzle task.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究用一个简单的拼图任务检验挫折与攻击的假说。
senses.why: A research programme gave the everyday feeling a technical definition so it could be measured.
senses.whyCN: 一个研究纲领给日常感受下了技术定义，好让它能被测量。

senses.title: Frustration of a contract
senses.definition: in law, the ending of an agreement because an unforeseen event makes performance impossible
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，因不可预见的事件使履行成为不可能而终止协议
senses.example: The storm led to the frustration of the shipping contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴导致运输合同落空。
senses.why: The legal use keeps the old sense of making an obligation vain without anyone being at fault.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留了古老的意思：在无人有过错的情况下使义务变成空文。

senses.title: The point where a learner gives up
senses.definition: in education, the level of difficulty at which a student stops trying
senses.definitionCN: 在教育中，学生停止努力的那个难度水平
senses.example: Reading tasks were kept just below the frustration level.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读任务的难度被控制在挫败临界点之下。
senses.why: Teaching borrows the word for the moment when challenge stops being productive and becomes a wall.
senses.whyCN: 教学借这个词指挑战不再有成效、变成一堵墙的那一刻。

intro.en: Frustration comes from the Latin noun for a disappointment, built on an adverb meaning 'in vain'. The original picture is an effort that comes to nothing.
intro.cn: frustration 来自拉丁语中指「失望」的名词，它由意为「徒然」的副词构成。原始画面是一次落空的努力。

items.en: Frustra was an adverb meaning 'in vain, to no purpose'. It is the seed of the whole family and already contains the idea of wasted effort.
items.cn: frustra 是副词，意为「徒然、无结果」。它是整个词族的种子，本身已经含有「努力被浪费」的意思。

items.en: The verb frustrari meant 'to disappoint, deceive, bring to nothing'. It could describe both a failed attempt and a deliberate act of defeating someone.
items.cn: 动词 frustrari 意为「使失望、欺骗、使成空」。它既能描述失败的尝试，也能描述刻意使某人落空的行为。

items.en: The noun frustratio named a disappointment or a deception, and this is the form that passed into English.
items.cn: 名词 frustratio 指失望或欺骗，进入英语的正是这个形式。

items.en: English adopted the noun in the seventeenth century in the sense of defeating a design, and the psychological sense grew from that use.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪接受了这个名词，意为使计谋失败；心理学义就从这个用法生长出来。

items.en: Psychologists made the word a technical term for a blocked goal, and later borrowed it for the difficulty level at which learners stop working.
items.cn: 心理学家把这个词变成指「目标受阻」的术语，后来又借它指学习者停止努力的难度水平。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link sometimes proposed between the 'in vain' adverb and the Latin word for fraud is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation, and the deeper origin is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：有人提出「徒然」副词与拉丁语中指欺诈的词之间有联系，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生，更深来源也无定论。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same word that are regularly mixed up; the second holds other words for being stopped short.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式，常被混用；第二组是其他表示「被挡住」的词。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: it describes the person who feels the block, not the block itself.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词用作形容词：描写感到受阻的人，而非阻碍本身。

entries.definition: The present participle: it describes the thing or task that produces the feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词：描写产生这种感受的事物或任务。

entries.definition: The base verb: to block someone's aim, or, in law, to make an agreement impossible to perform.
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词：阻碍某人的目标；在法律中指使协议无法履行。

entries.definition: From a Latin word for deceit; the resemblance to the 'in vain' family is misleading and the two are usually treated as separate roots.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语中指欺骗的词；与「徒然」词族的相似是误导，两者通常被视为不同词根。

entries.definition: It focuses on a result falling short of hope, with no emphasis on a barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 侧重结果不及期望，不强调有障碍。

entries.definition: It implies an outside agent actively defeating a plan, close to the oldest sense of frustration.
entries.definitionCN: 暗含外部力量主动挫败计划，接近 frustration 最古老的意思。

entries.definition: Concrete and physical: something is stuck in a passage, with no emotional content.
entries.definitionCN: 具体而物理：有东西堵在通道里，不含情绪成分。

entries.definition: It names the surface anger alone, while frustration keeps the cause of the anger in view.
entries.definitionCN: 只指表层的恼怒，而 frustration 始终把恼怒的成因留在视野里。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin adverb behind the word means 'in vain', so frustration is literally effort made vain.
normal.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁副词意为「徒然」，所以 frustration 字面上就是「被弄成徒劳的努力」。

normal.en: The family runs frustrate, frustrated, frustrating, frustratingly, frustration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 frustrate、frustrated、frustrating、frustratingly、frustration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the target: frustration with a person, frustration at a delay, in frustration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：对某人的不满、对延误的不满、气恼地。

normal.en: Law uses the phrase for a contract that an unforeseen event makes impossible to perform.
normal.cn: 法律用这个词组指因不可预见事件而无法履行的合同。

normal.en: Education speaks of a frustration level, the difficulty at which a learner stops trying.
normal.cn: 教育学讲「挫败水平」，即学习者停止尝试的那个难度。

abstract.en: Picture a screw turning forever because the thread is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗永远在转、因为螺纹已经磨平的螺丝。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens inward every time you push outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇你往外推、它却往里开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle with the lid held down while the water boils.
abstract.cn: 想象水在沸腾，壶盖却被按住了。

examples.en: He slammed the folder shut in frustration and walked out.
examples.cn: 他气恼地把文件夹合上，走了出去。

examples.en: The delay caused growing frustration among passengers.
examples.cn: 延误在乘客中引起了越来越深的挫败感。

examples.en: Therapy helped her separate frustration from the person she was angry with.
examples.cn: 治疗帮助她把挫败感与那个让她生气的人分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: frustr（徒然）+ ation（状态）＝ 力气使出去却什么都没成 → 挫败感、挫折。

root: 拉丁 frustratio「失望、使成空」，来自 frustrari「使徒劳、使失望」，再上溯副词 frustra「徒然」。frustra 更深来源不确定，与拉丁语中指欺诈的词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one empty result: an effort made vain. The result can be felt, named as an obstacle, caused by someone, stretched over years, turned into temper, made a research variable, written into a contract, or measured as a limit in a classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个空结果展开：被弄成徒劳的努力。这个结果可以被感受到、被指为障碍、被某人造成、拉成多年经历、转成脾气、变成研究变量、写进合同，或被量成教室里的一个界限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a door that will not open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手推着一扇打不开的门。

chain: A RULE THAT ENDS THE TRYING

branches.en: ONE FEELING, TWO LENGTHS: a single blocked moment, and the same moment repeated until it becomes an era.
branches.cn: 一种感受、两种长度：一次受阻的瞬间，以及同一瞬间重复到成为一段岁月。

branches.en: THE WALL AND WHO BUILT IT: the obstacle as a thing, then the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 墙与造墙的人：先看作为物的障碍，再看把墙立起来的那一举。

branches.en: PRESSURE WITH NO OUTLET: energy that cannot reach the goal turns into temper.
branches.cn: 无处可去的压力：到不了目标的力量转成脾气。

branches.en: MEASURED TWICE: once as a variable in a laboratory, once as the line where a student stops.
branches.cn: 被测量两次：一次作为实验室变量，一次作为学生停手的那条线。

branches.en: WRITTEN INTO LAW: an obligation made empty by events nobody caused.
branches.cn: 写进法律：无人造成的事件把义务变成空文。

intro.en: Frustration is formed from the Latin noun of action, and the same stem supplies the verb and both participles that English uses as adjectives.
intro.cn: frustration 由拉丁语的表动作名词构成，同一词干还提供英语用作形容词的两个分词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family turns on an adverb meaning 'in vain'; from it come the verb, the noun of action and the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个拉丁词族围绕一个意为「徒然」的副词展开；由它产生动词、表动作名词与英语动词。

items.example: The adverb states the outcome before anything happens.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在事情发生前就说出了结果。

items.example: The attempt was made and brought to nothing.
items.exampleCN: 那番尝试做出来，又被弄成了空。

items.example: The noun names the outcome, not the effort.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指结果，而非努力。

items.structure: frustrate (English verb, from the Latin participle)
items.example: Poor planning frustrated the whole project.
items.exampleCN: 规划不当让整个项目受挫。

items.example: The frustrated driver stopped the engine.
items.exampleCN: 那位受挫的司机熄了火。

items.example: The frustrating part was the missing page.
items.exampleCN: 让人恼火的是那一页不见了。

items.example: Frustration built up over three weeks.
items.exampleCN: 挫败感在三周里积累起来。

items.example: Frustratingly, the file was saved on another machine.
items.exampleCN: 令人气恼的是，文件存在另一台机器上。

latinEntries.structure: frustrari, frustratus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

derivatives.zh: 使受挫；使落空（拉丁动词「使成为徒劳」直接进入英语）
受挫的；沮丧的（动词过去分词转为形容词）
令人挫败的（动词现在分词转为形容词，指引起这种感受）
令人气恼地（分词形容词加副词后缀）
